title: Topology and geometric fibres of an adequate moduli space
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ an adequate moduli space of an algebraic stack over $k$ [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]. Assume, as in Alper's Section 2 conventions, that the diagonals of $\mathcal X$ and $Y$ over $k$ are quasi-compact and separated: each scheme test of either diagonal is an algebraic space whose structural morphism is quasi-compact and whose relative diagonal is a closed immersion. Then $\phi$ is universally submersive: after every base change $Y'\to Y$ by an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space], the map $|\mathcal X\times_Y Y'|\to|Y'|$ is surjective and a subset of $|Y'|$ is open if and only if its inverse image is open. For every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$, the map from isomorphism classes of $\Omega$-objects of $\mathcal X$ to $Y(\Omega)$ is surjective, and $\phi(x_1)=\phi(x_2)$ if and only if the closures of $x_1$ and $x_2$ in $|\mathcal X_\Omega|$ intersect. Here $\mathcal X_\Omega=\mathcal X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$; points and their closures are taken in the usual underlying topological space of the algebraic stack, obtained from a smooth atlas with its quotient topology. No finite-type or reducedness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For any algebraic-space base change $Y'\to Y$, let $p:|\mathcal X\times_Y Y'|\to|Y'|$. [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-universally-submersive] states exactly that $p$ is surjective and that a subset $V\subseteq|Y'|$ is open if and only if $p^{-1}(V)$ is open; that node imposes no diagonal hypothesis on $Y'$, so this proves universal submersiveness for arbitrary $Y'$, including ones without quasi-compact diagonal. Step 3 also uses the surjectivity and the closedness itself: [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-topological-images] states that $p$ sends closed subsets to closed subsets for every morphism of algebraic spaces $Y'\to Y$. Neither assertion says that $\phi_{Y'}$ is adequate.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.1(1)--(3): the closed-surjection argument, carried by the existing universal-submersiveness node.

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$. Apply [lem-sfb-adequate-flat-base-change] to $Y_\Omega\to Y$. This map is flat: on affine charts its ring map is $A\to A\otimes_k\Omega$, and tensoring along it is tensoring the underlying $k$-module with the vector space $\Omega$, which is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat, lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. The diagonal hypotheses persist under this scalar base change. Thus $\phi_\Omega:\mathcal X_\Omega\to Y_\Omega$ is adequate. The identification of its source with $\mathcal X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and the correspondence between $k$-morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\mathcal X$ and $\Omega$-objects of this source follow by unpacking the $2$-fibre-product data.

For $y\in Y(\Omega)$, the fibre $\mathcal F=\mathcal X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is nonempty by Step 1. Quasi-compactness of $\phi$ gives a quasi-compact smooth atlas of $\mathcal F$ by the definition [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Its diagonal is the corresponding base change of the relative diagonal of $\phi$, so is quasi-compact; it is separated because the diagonal of $\mathcal X/k$ is separated. Step 1's closedness assertion after every further scheme base change supplies the universally closed hypothesis of [lem-sfb-universally-closed-stack-rational-point]. This node gives an object of $\mathcal F(\Omega)$; its projection is an object $x$ with $\phi(x)=y$. Thus the asserted map on isomorphism classes is surjective over this very field.

source.place: Same-field existence input, with universal closedness supplied by Theorem 5.3.1(2).

proof.text: Put $C_i=\overline{\{[x_i]\}}\subset|\mathcal X_\Omega|$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets] they carry reduced closed substacks $\mathcal C_i$. By [lem-sfb-qs-space-rational-point-topology] the image point $y_i=\phi_\Omega(x_i)$ is closed in $|Y_\Omega|$, and distinct $\Omega$-points give distinct underlying points. Continuity gives $\phi_\Omega(C_i)\subseteq\overline{\{[y_i]\}}=\{[y_i]\}$; as $x_i\in C_i$, equality holds. Apply the intersection formula of [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-topological-images] to $\phi_\Omega$ and the two closed substacks. If $y_1=y_2$, the left side of that formula is the nonempty singleton $\{[y_1]\}$, hence $C_1\cap C_2$ is nonempty; here the $2$-fibre-product point surjectivity in the smooth-presentation node identifies the intersection with the image of $|\mathcal C_1\times_{\mathcal X_\Omega}\mathcal C_2|$. Conversely a point of $C_1\cap C_2$ maps to both $[y_1]$ and $[y_2]$, and injectivity in the rational-point node gives $y_1=y_2$ as $\Omega$-points. This is the claimed equivalence; it also shows closure intersection defines an equivalence relation, since equality of images does.
